text: I think people often misunderstand the debate over standardized testing. Critics are right that over-reliance on test scores narrows the curriculum and creates perverse incentives. But supporters have a valid point too: without some form of standardized measurement, it becomes very difficult to identify schools where students are falling behind, particularly in low-income districts where parents may have less political power to demand accountability. The question isn't whether to test or not to test — it's how to design assessments that provide useful information without distorting what happens in classrooms.
